title: Quarterly strategy sprint: agenda, stakeholder asks, and decision ledger
content:
Purpose and framing:
This doc is a compact, timeboxed QBR format designed as a 'strategy sprint'—goal is to leave with 3 prioritized customer asks, 2 measurable commitments (owner + date), and a small decision ledger recording tradeoffs and next steps. Use when there are multiple stakeholders and the account requires clarity for renewal conversations or product prioritization.

Meeting length: 45 minutes (recommended) or 30 minutes (condensed).
Audience: CSM, Customer sponsor (product/ops), Technical champion, Solutions engineer (optional), Renewal owner (if different).

Pre-meeting prework (send 5 business days before):
- 5-minute survey link to customer: top 3 business priorities next 90 days, top friction points, $$/SLO risk flag (yes/no).
- CSM: fill pre-read one-pager (1 page): current usage, product surface touched, top incidents since last QBR, NPS/CSAT snapshot, renewal window.
- SE: short status of integrations (bullet list) + any open P1/P2 tickets.
- From Redwood: send short slide with usage trend (30/60/90 days) and cost-per-query comparison vs previous quarter.

Agenda (45m) — timeboxes and facilitation cues:
1) 0:00–0:05 — Kickoff and outcomes (Facilitator)
   - Quick hello, confirm attendees and time remaining.
   - Read out meeting outcomes: Align on 3 prioritized asks, capture 2 commitments, identify renewal risk.
   - Cue: "If we only achieve one thing today, it should be..." (ask customer to state).

2) 0:05–0:15 — Current state snapshot (CSM + SE, 2 slides max)
   - One slide: adoption highlights (key flows, top teams using product).
   - One slide: friction and incidents + mitigations.
   - Facilitation script: "We’ll run the data for 2 minutes, then I want your top reaction — what's missing from this view?"

3) 0:15–0:30 — Opportunity mapping and prioritization sprint (interactive)
   - Method: 10m silent brainstorm (customer + Redwood) using shared doc; each person adds 1–3 'asks' (feature, support, ops change, enablement).
   - 5m cluster and dot-vote (CSM facilitates, add ticks in doc).
   - 5m quick tradeoff discussion: impact vs effort.
   - Output: top 3 asks with rationale.

4) 0:30–0:40 — Decision ledger and commitment capture (Facilitator + Owners)
   - For each top ask, use Decision Template: Decision ID / Brief / Owner / Due Date / Acceptance Criteria / Dependencies / Risk (1-3).
   - Ask customer: which ask is priority for renewal discussions? Record as 'renewal signal'.
   - Facilitation script: "Who at the customer will sign off? Who at Redwood will deliver? Let’s lock owners and dates now."

5) 0:40–0:45 — Next steps, escalation lanes, and micro-retro
   - Confirm follow-up items and owners; schedule 30-min ops check if any technical deliverable is >2 weeks out.
   - Micro-retro: 1 thing we should stop, 1 thing we should start, 1 thing we should continue. Capture in notes.

Facilitator playbook (short snippets you can read):
- Opening: "Thanks for the time—my objective is to make sure you get clarity on roadmap impact and our mutual priorities for the next 90 days. I’ll keep us tight on time and call for a decision if needed."
- When the convo stalls: "We have two paths: A) do a short spike and reconvene in 2 weeks, or B) commit to a scoped deliverable by [date]. Which works better for you?"
- If exec asks for numbers: "We’ll follow up with a tailored cost/perf snapshot within 48 hours; for decisions here we’ll use the qualitative prioritization and capture any number requests as action items."

Decision ledger template (paste into notes doc as a table):
- Decision ID: D-2026-01
- Summary: Authorize dedicated throughput increase for Search API
- Owner: Redwood SE (Liam O'Connor) / Customer Ops (J. Ramirez)
- Due date: 2026-02-05
- Acceptance criteria: 20% latency reduction in peak window; cost delta <= 12%
- Dependencies: infra quota increase, customer sign-off on scoped test user set
- Risk rating: Medium

Renewal signal glossary (use to mark meeting outcome):
- Green: No blockers, adoption trending up, renewal likelihood > 80% (no action required beyond standard ops).
- Yellow: 1–2 medium blockers, adoption flat, require 2 tactical commitments to improve health.
- Red: Critical blockers exist (incidents, security, data residency), require exec intervention/in-person review.

Quick checklist for CSM before sending meeting notes (post-meeting):
- Create a one-page summary with top 3 asks and decisions.
- Populate Decision ledger in shared folder and assign watchers.
- Open JIRA tickets for any Redwood delivery items; link them in the follow-up.
- Send calendar invite for check-in(s) and set reminder 7 days before each due date.

Escalation lanes (if status=Red):
- Step 1: Elevation to CS Manager (within 24 hours) + exec summary.
- Step 2: If unresolved after 72 hours, schedule a triage with Product + Infra + Customer Ops.
- Step 3: If still unresolved after 7 days, route to Commercial lead for renewal conversation.

Notes on evidence and artifacts to include in follow-up packet:
- Short adoption waterfall: users by team, weekly active context, top 10 invoked endpoints.
- Cost per inference trend and example queries that spike cost.
- Incident timeline with root cause and mitigation status.
- Attach the 5-min customer pre-survey summary.

Optional condensed 30-minute flow (for exec-only):
- 0:00–0:06 Kickoff & outcomes
- 0:06–0:12 Top metrics (adoption, incidents, cost delta)
- 0:12–0:22 Top 2 asks (presented with tradeoff table)
- 0:22–0:28 Commitments and owners
- 0:28–0:30 Wrap and confirm next touchpoint

Templates to paste into notes (copy-paste friendly)
- Action: [Short description] | Owner: [name] | Due: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Acceptance: [metric/criteria]
- Decision: [short summary] | Owner: [name] | Outcome: [Approve/Defer/Decline] | Rationale: [1-2 lines]

Common failure modes and facilitator responses:
- Failure: Customer asks for a full roadmap review (time sink). Response: "We can schedule a deep roadmap session; for this sprint let’s surface the 1–2 items that matter for your renewal decision and capture roadmap asks as follow-ups."
- Failure: Multiple stakeholders disagree on priority. Response: "Let’s capture both options and agree on a short pilot for 2 weeks with measurable success criteria — will that resolve the disagreement?"

Post-meeting health check cadence recommendation:
- If signal=Green: biweekly usage summary email + quarterly follow-up.
- If signal=Yellow: 2-week ops check + monthly steward review.
- If signal=Red: weekly cross-functional triage + exec sync until resolved.

Appendix: sample 3 prioritized asks (realistic examples to seed brainstorm)
- Ask A: Dedicated throughput bump for Search API for holiday peak (Owner: Redwood SE)
- Ask B: Custom embedding model re-tuning to reduce hallucination on product taxonomy (Owner: Product + Applied ML)
- Ask C: SSO integration enforcement and audit log delivery for compliance (Owner: Private Deployments PM)

Document history and quick notes:
- 2025-11-12: created by Aisha Patel (first-pass sprint agenda)
- 2026-01-15: added decision ledger template and escalation lanes (Marco Diaz)
- 2026-02-20: refined prework and condensed 30-min flow (Sofia Nguyen)

End of doc.
